leaders.notes: Listed as Aurora University's 12th president (1988-2000), preceding Rebecca Sherrick. Independent corroboration beyond a single aggregator (Plexuss) and consistency with the university's own numbering of Sherrick as 13th president was not found; treat name/dates as best-effort and re-verify in a later backfill pass.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost (and faculty member, women's studies program founder)
leaders.notes: 13th president; 22-23 year tenure, second-longest in AU history. Doubled undergraduate enrollment and oversaw the 2000 Aurora University/George Williams College merger. Went on to serve as interim president of Saint Xavier University from July 2023 until Keith Elder took office in March 2024.

leaders.priorInstitution: Northern Kentucky University (prior senior roles at Ball State University and Oregon State University)
leaders.notes: 14th president of Aurora University; first Latina to lead the institution. Began her tenure in 2023.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President of the College (also held Dean of Student Affairs and Executive Assistant to the President roles)
leaders.notes: 27th president of Baker University; served 19 years, one of the longest tenures in school history, retiring at the end of the 2005-06 academic year.

leaders.priorTitle: Acting Executive Vice Chancellor / Vice Chancellor for Student Affairs and Enrollment Management
leaders.notes: 28th president; Baker's first woman president in its 150+ year history. Inaugurated October 2006, announced retirement effective June 2014.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President of Development, Alumni and International Relations
leaders.notes: 29th president, began July 1, 2014. Announced departure to become McMurry University's 11th president, starting there January 10, 2025; left Baker at the end of 2024.

Baker alumnus (BA 1973) and longtime trustee appointed acting/interim president in October 2024 to bridge the gap while the university searched for a permanent successor to Lynne Murray; served until Jody Fournier took office July 1, 2025. Full legal first name behind the nickname "Hoot" was not found in public sources.
31st president of Baker University, effective July 1, 2025.

5th president of Barry University, serving 23 years (1981-2004), one of the longest presidencies in the nation at the time. After stepping down she served as Barry's chancellor for five years and became president emerita in 2009. Died in 2019 at age 90.

6th president and first Barry alumna to hold the role; inaugurated November 2004, served through July 2019. Previously held several roles at Barry itself (dean, associate VP for academic affairs) before leaving in 1986 and later leading Gwynedd-Mercy College.

leaders.priorInstitution: The Catholic University of America (Washington, DC)
leaders.notes: 7th president, took office July 1, 2019; first man and first layperson to lead Barry University since its 1940 founding.

leaders.priorInstitution: Bastyr University (formerly John Bastyr College of Naturopathic Medicine)
leaders.notes: Founding president, served 22 years (1978-2000). Returned decades later as interim president twice more (see below).
Second president of Bastyr University; unexpectedly resigned in 2004 after about four years in office.

Served roughly a decade as president, retiring effective June 30, 2015. A short gap year (2004-05) between Shepherd's resignation and Church's start, and a roughly two-year gap (2015-2017) between Church's retirement and Harlan Patterson's interim appointment, could not be attributed to a named leader from available public sources; this window likely involved unnamed interim/acting leadership.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice Chancellor for Finance and Administration, University of Washington Tacoma (also Bastyr Board of Trustees member for ~6 years)
leaders.notes: Began as interim president in July 2017 (having served on Bastyr's Board of Trustees), was unanimously appointed permanent president in April 2018, and served through the transition to Devin Byrd in mid-2021.
Sixth president and Bastyr's first African American president; started July 26, 2021. Oversaw pandemic-era campus reopening and expansion of online programs. Departed in mid-2025.
Founding president returned as interim president in 2025 following Devin Byrd's departure, to lead the university through its next presidential transition.
